name: flag-hoist-run
title: Flag Hoist Run
description: An ambient in-flight/queue-depth status card modelled on a mechanical flag hoist: small flags climb a halyard, break out into a flying position at the yard, then are struck down fast to clear the line for the next hoist.
useWhen: a background status card standing in for a generic loader/spinner where the point is continuous, in-flight queue depth over time rather than a single value or a finished process — how many items are currently in flight reads as how many chips are on the line at once. Reach for queue-triage-ratchet instead when the surface is a one-card-at-a-time decision queue driven by user input, not an ambient background indicator; reach for toast-gravity-stack instead when the mechanic is a single item's arrival and dismissal into a heap, not a continuous mechanical cycle with no discrete start/end.
instruction: Build <FlagHoistRun className?> as a self-contained, non-interactive DOM/SVG-free (plain divs) ambient status widget inside a bordered card (rounded-md border border-border bg-surface, fixed 4:3 aspect-ratio, overflow-hidden). It renders a single vertical halyard line running from y=92% of card height (the deck) to y=8% (the yard), plus a short horizontal yard tick at y=8%, both var(--foreground) at a fixed 0.3 opacity, 1.5px thick — never var(--border), which falls to ~1.1:1 contrast in light theme and would read as invisible rather than a taut line. A fixed pool of 4 flag-chip divs (never more are mounted; MAX_CHIPS=4 comfortably covers ceil(4200ms cycle / 1300ms stagger)) are mutated directly every animation frame via refs (style.left/top/width/height/transform only — no React state per frame, so the ~14 hoists/minute this produces at typical concurrency never re-render React). Each chip is a solid var(--foreground) rectangle, width = 0.24x and height = 0.11x the container's SMALLER measured dimension (so it rescales correctly at card scale), left edge pinned to the halyard's x (50% of width) with transform-origin left center so all motion pivots off that attachment point. CYCLE (per chip, driven by performance.now() minus that chip's own spawn timestamp, not modulo'd against a shared clock): a 2400ms climb at constant velocity from y=92% to y=8% while rotated -90deg around the left-edge pivot (the folded state — an edge-on rectangle reads as a narrow vertical sliver flush against the halyard, exactly as a furled flag hugs the line on its way up, no separate width/scale hack needed since the rotation alone does it); a 300ms break-out easing (easeOutCubic) rotation from -90deg to 0deg at a fixed y=8% (the yard) — the one moment that has to read as a distinct 'arrival', a full rectangle swinging out to horizontal, not a continuation of the climb; an 1100ms fly holding rotation at 0deg, full silhouette, at the yard; then a 400ms strike (easeInCubic, deliberately faster than the 2400ms climb so it reads as a quick, separate mechanical action) translating y from 8% down to 118% — past the card's overflow-hidden bottom edge, so the chip genuinely 'drops out of view' via clipping rather than a fade. Full individual cycle: 2400+300+1100+400=4200ms. A new chip begins climbing from the deck every 1300ms (a fixed 4-slot round-robin, each slot idling ~1000ms between its own 4200ms hoists), so 1-2 chips are typically climbing at once while at most one flies at the yard at a time — queue depth reads directly as how many chips are currently on the line. TOKENS: colors are CSS custom properties referenced directly as `var(--foreground)` in inline styles (pure DOM, no canvas, so no getComputedStyle/MutationObserver token-read dance is needed — the cascade repaints for free on a theme class flip). No --ns-accent anywhere; this is a resting, non-interactive ambient surface, not a control. REDUCED MOTION: freezes on the single most structured static frame available in the cycle — one chip parked mid-climb at exactly 50% up the mast (rotation -90deg) and a second chip simultaneously parked flying at the yard (rotation 0deg, y=8%), both states visible at once, remaining two pool slots hidden, no rAF loop ever started. A ResizeObserver re-measures the container (and re-renders the reduced-motion frame, or arms the rAF loop, accordingly) on layout change; an IntersectionObserver pauses the rAF loop when the card scrolls off-screen and re-arms it on re-entry. Cleanup on unmount cancels any pending rAF and disconnects both observers. No pointer interaction of any kind — ambient only.
